questions.question_text: Explain the working of a convolutional neural network for image classification.
questions.expected_answer: Convolution layers slide learned filters over the image to produce feature maps that detect local patterns; non-linear activations follow; pooling layers downsample feature maps, reducing computation and adding translation tolerance; stacked layers learn increasingly abstract features; fully connected layers map the final features to class scores, usually through softmax.

rubric.expected_evidence: Explains that filters slide over the input to produce feature maps detecting local patterns.
Explains pooling reduces spatial size and that deeper layers capture more abstract features.
Explains fully connected layer(s) turning features into class scores or probabilities.
Steps are in a sensible order.

answers.text: A CNN passes small learned filters (kernels) across the image. Each filter produces a feature map that is high where its pattern, like an edge, appears. After a ReLU, max pooling shrinks each map so the network is cheaper and tolerant to small shifts. Stacking these layers lets early layers find edges and later layers find shapes and objects. Finally the maps are flattened and fully connected layers with softmax give the probability of each class.

Think of it as a set of pattern detectors. Each detector is a tiny window of weights we move over the picture, and wherever it matches we get a strong response, giving a response grid. Grids are then summarised by taking the biggest value in each small block, which makes them smaller. Doing this repeatedly builds up from lines to parts to whole objects, and a final dense layer votes on the label.
CNN uses convolution layers where a filter moves over the image and makes feature maps. Then there is a fully connected layer that gives the output class.

A CNN is a recurrent network that reads the image pixel by pixel in sequence and remembers previous pixels. Pooling increases the size of the image so that more detail is kept. The last layer is a convolution that outputs the class.

Filters slide over the image to give feature maps. Pooling reduces the size of the feature maps. Pooling also makes the feature maps larger so no information is lost. A dense layer gives class scores.

questions.question_text: Describe the ACID properties of a database transaction.
questions.expected_answer: Atomicity: all operations happen or none. Consistency: a transaction moves the database between valid states respecting constraints. Isolation: concurrent transactions do not see each other's intermediate state. Durability: committed changes survive failures.

rubric.expected_evidence: All-or-nothing execution; committed data survives crashes.
Constraints preserved; concurrent transactions do not interfere.

answers.text: Atomic means a transfer either fully happens or is rolled back. Consistent means constraints like balances never going negative still hold after it. Isolated means two transfers at once behave as if they ran one after the other. Durable means once committed it is saved even if the server crashes.
Atomicity means all or nothing. Durability means data is not lost after commit.
